title: Part (c): unspecified constants and a hidden strong spectral-gap hypothesis (thm:precision)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**[proof-gap | RIGOR/SCOPE]** `thm:precision`, `eq:fperr`, `eq:precregime`, `eq:keff`.

1. The backward-error constants $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are 'low polynomial degree in $m,n,\ell$' but never written, yet both `eq:fperr` and the boundary `eq:precregime` depend on them. Pin them via Higham Thm 3.5 (matrix multiply), Thm 19.4 (Householder QR), and Demmel-Kahan (backward-stable SVD).
2. The rank-$k$ truncation step bounds the gap $g\ge(\sigma_k-\sigma_{k+1})-2\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\tau_k$ and then **assumes** $\sigma_k-\sigma_{k+1}\ge 4\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\tau_k$. In the heavy-tail regime $\tau_k\gg\sigma_1$ this fails for essentially all matrices, so `eq:precregime` holds only under a restrictive spectral hypothesis. Make it a stated hypothesis or analyze the small-gap regime separately via the $1/(\sigma_k-\sigma_{k+1})$ amplification in $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
3. The Wedin $\sin\Theta$ bound uses the separation/gap of the unperturbed $\widehat Q^\top A$; the standard separation hypothesis must be checked explicitly to justify the non-Lipschitz projector perturbation term $c_2 u\,\sigma_1/\sigma_{\min}(A\Omega)\,\|A\|_F$.
